name: Chevron Federal Credit Union
desc:
Member Experience Specialist | $16.97 to $23.33/hr (Zone 3) plus quarterly incentives | Inbound Member Service with Cross-Selling Goals
Company: Chevron Federal Credit Union
Industry: Finance

What Your Day Will Look Like:
Chevron Federal Credit Union is one of the largest credit unions in the country, with $5 billion in assets. In this role, you work in their virtual call center taking calls from members and people interested in joining. You'll answer questions about accounts, products, and services, and handle more complex requests across teams like Lending, ATM and Debit Cards, Online and Mobile Banking, Foreign Currency, Wires, and outbound service calls. You'll process transactions like fee reversals, transfers, loan payments, address updates, check orders, and stop payments, and send forms securely. Part of the job is spotting when a member could use another product or service and making referrals or opening accounts, with individual growth targets. You'll document every call in their CRM, help train other agents on Zoom, and keep up with security training and company updates. This is an intermediate level role, so they want people who already have call center experience.

Soft Skills
- Active listening
- Patience and empathy
- Problem solving and good judgment
- Confidence recommending products
- Adaptability to change

skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements

Education Minimum: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent
Required Experience: 2 to 5 years of call center experience. An equivalent mix of education and experience may substitute.
Preferred Experience: None listed beyond the requirements

Required Skills:
- Clear written and spoken English with correct spelling and grammar
- Active listening and matching the member's sense of urgency
- Basic math, including rates, ratios, and percentages using a 10-key
- Typing at 40 wpm
- Comfortable with Outlook, Word, Excel, and Zoom
- Familiar with CRM and document storage systems
- Keeps member information confidential
- Strong attendance

This role is ideal for someone who:
- Has 2+ years of call center experience, especially in banking or finance
- Is comfortable suggesting products when it truly helps the member
- Is good with numbers and quick on a 10-key
- Wants strong benefits and room to grow with a large credit union

Not a Good Fit for someone who:
- Has less than 2 years of call center experience
- Isn't comfortable with sales goals or product referrals
- Struggles with attendance
- Prefers simple, script-only calls over complex requests
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
1. Apply online
2. Application review: the team checks your application against the qualifications
3. Screening and assessment: a recruiter reaches out for a phone screen and skills assessment (typing, basic math, ratios, percentages, and 10-key)
4. Interviews: depending on the role, a series of interviews, mostly on Zoom
5. Offer
6. Background check: satisfactory results are required
7. Welcome to the team
This is the process listed on Chevron FCU's careers page.

Interview Tips
- Download Zoom ahead of time and get familiar with it
- Use a quiet, well-lit, clean space and dress business casual
- Keep your computer charged or plugged in
- Review their core competencies and be ready for behavior-based questions with real examples
- Bring a few questions to ask about the role or team

Top 10 Resume Keywords
- Call center
- Member service
- Financial transactions
- Account maintenance
- Cross-selling and referrals
- 10-key
- CRM documentation
- Problem resolution and escalation
- Banking products and services
- Confidentiality and compliance

4-5 Interview Questions for this Role:
- Tell us about your call center experience and the types of calls you handled.
- How would you suggest a new product to a member without it feeling like a sales pitch?
- A member is upset about a fee on their account. Walk us through how you'd handle it.
- Tell us about a time you solved a complex customer problem. What was the problem, what did you do, and what was the result?
- Tell us about a time you met or beat a goal at work. What was the goal, what did you do, and what was the result?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
-Pay: Based on location zone. Zone 3 is $16.97 to $23.33/hr. Other zones: Zone 1 $20.20 to $27.78, Zone 2 $18.38 to $25.28, Zone 4 $16.16 to $22.22. Plus quarterly incentives based on member surveys, service metrics, sales, and new money growth.
-Shift: Must have availability for any shift based on business needs. Can be discussed in final interview, offer stage.
-Benefits: Bonus and incentives for all full-time employees, 401(k) with 8% company contribution, medical, dental, and vision for employees and dependents covered at 80%, PTO starting at 18 days a year, paid sabbaticals, fully paid short and long term disability, fully paid life and AD&D insurance at two times annual salary, and tuition reimbursement.
-Equipment Provided: Not stated in the posting. Ask in the interview.
-Felony Friendly?: No, per our current listing. A satisfactory background check is required.
-Drug Test: Certain positions
-Notes: This is an evergreen posting. There isn't an immediate opening, but they hire for this role regularly, and applying now gets you considered as soon as a spot opens. The benefits are excellent, especially the 8% 401(k) contribution and 18 days of PTO to start. Expect individual sales and growth goals along with service work. They use E-Verify. Training length and camera requirements are not listed.
-Career Pathway: Reasonable inferred path: Member Experience Specialist → Senior Member Experience Specialist → Call Center Team Lead → Call Center Supervisor → Call Center Manager. This role builds banking product knowledge, financial transaction, and member relationship skills.

Participant-Reported Assessment Info (from past applicants, may vary):
- A HireVue on-demand video interview may come first, with availability, customer service, and behavioral questions. A smartphone may work if you don't have a webcam.
- An online assessment may follow right after: a timed cognitive section (about 50 questions in 12 minutes covering logic, patterns, verbal reasoning, and basic math), a career interest section (about 55 questions), and a personality section (about 150 agree or disagree questions).
- Tips: test in a quiet space, read timed questions carefully, answer personality questions honestly and consistently, and review their mission and values first.
training: Discussed in interview-Must have flexible availability
